I’m genuinely fed up with ChatGPT’s image editing.

A simple request to add a small cross necklace to an existing image, without changing anything else, has turned into an exhausting exercise in frustration.

Around 45 out of 50 attempts result in some ridiculous warning about scam activity, despite the request having absolutely nothing to do with scams, fraud, or anything remotely suspicious.

On the rare occasions the request actually gets through, the model still manages to get it wrong. It changes parts of the image that I specifically instructed it to leave untouched.

The instructions couldn’t be clearer: Do not alter anything. Just add the necklace.

Yet somehow, this basic task becomes a battle against false safety warnings, inconsistent results, and a model that seemingly cannot follow straightforward instructions.

What’s particularly infuriating is the amount of time wasted repeating the same request over and over, trying to get something that should have worked the first time.

This isn’t a complicated editing job. It’s adding one small accessory to a picture.

If a paid AI service cannot reliably distinguish a harmless image edit from scam activity, and then cannot follow basic instructions when it finally allows the edit, there is a serious problem with both its moderation system and its image-editing capabilities.

I’m not asking for miracles. I’m asking for the service to do what it’s told without falsely flagging innocent requests or unnecessarily altering the original image.

At this point, the experience feels less like using a helpful AI tool and more like fighting against the software just to accomplish the simplest task.

One star. Not because the technology lacks potential, but because the actual user experience is unbelievably frustrating.

I’m genuinely considering deleting this app after how frustrating my experience has become.

I use ChatGPT for creative projects that genuinely matter to me, including making pictures and posters for my Facebook gifting group. I enjoy being able to send pictures, show products, keep track of prices and work with ChatGPT to create things I’m excited about.

But lately, I’m constantly running into restrictions that stop me from doing what I came here to do. I can’t always send pictures, I run into limits on how much I can use it, and it feels like every time I want to get something done, there’s another barrier in the way.

Today has been the final straw. I was preparing a Christmas Most Wanted poster, collecting items and prices so I could get it posted in time for an event starting at 8 pm, when people could help by finding and gifting the items. I had been working towards this all day, only to find that picture uploads were unavailable until much later than I’d expected.

I wasn’t expecting to have to plan my day around upload restrictions, and I wasn’t made aware of how much these limits could interfere with what I wanted to do. I understand that services may need usage limits, but when those limits disrupt something time-sensitive, it is incredibly frustrating.

What makes this worse is that I rely on the app for creative support and enjoy having longer conversations while working on projects. Having restrictions affect pictures, image creation and conversation length makes the experience feel increasingly limited.

I was already having a difficult day, and something that should have been enjoyable ended up causing me more stress. I shouldn’t have to fight with an app just to make a poster.

I know no app can offer unlimited usage, but the limits need to be clearer, more predictable and better communicated. Users should have a reasonable understanding of what they can do before investing time in a project.

Right now, I’m questioning whether it’s worth continuing to use ChatGPT at all. It’s disappointing because I genuinely enjoy what I can create with it when it works as expected.

Please improve the transparency around usage limits and give users a more reliable experience. People use this app for real projects, with real deadlines, and these restrictions can have a genuine impact.
